dedupe_keys.name: multiyear nekton abundance and biomass along living shorelines north carolina 2001 to 2024

description: This dataset harmonises nekton abundance and biomass from five studies over 20 years at 12 living shorelines in North Carolina, each paired with a natural marsh and in some cases a bulkhead. Stephanie Valdez, Rachel Gittman, Megan Geesin, Brandon Puckett, Mariko Polk, Carolyn Currin and Carter Smith published it as a data paper in Ecology in February 2026, listed in the NOAA Institutional Repository. Living shorelines combine restored salt marsh or oyster reef with rock or concrete breakwaters for erosion protection; the data record 62 species groups of crustaceans, molluscs and fish between 2001 and 2024 (49 at living shorelines, 49 in natural marshes and 5 at bulkheads), with counts, biomass where available, sampling method, and each shoreline's type, age and location. Coverage is coastal North Carolina. Format and access: data files with the open access data paper. Licence: CC-BY-4.0; free. Caveats: the five studies used different gear and methods, so the authors warn against direct catch comparisons across sites. It supports evaluating nature-based coastal protection against grey defences. Related catalogue records are the ACJV coastal marsh project database and the global mangrove hybrid defence study.
